title: Arunachal, Assam & Meghalaya: 15 Days from Tawang to the Living Root Bridges
meta_description: 15-day North East India itinerary: Dirang, Sela Pass, Tawang Monastery, Bumla, Kaziranga rhino safaris, Cherrapunji waterfalls, Mawlynnong and Dawki.
hero_alt: Mountain road in North East India
tagline: Monasteries above the clouds, one-horned rhinos and the wettest hills on earth
facts: Long mountain drives, rest days built in
intro: A grand circuit of India's least-crowded corner. You climb from the Brahmaputra plains through the orchid forests of Bhalukpong and the apple orchards of Dirang to Tawang, home of India's largest monastery, then come down to Kaziranga for rhinos and elephants, and finish in Meghalaya's waterfalls, caves and living root bridges. The route climbs gradually, with two nights in Dirang before Tawang, so your body has time to adjust to the altitude.
highlights: Tawang Monastery, the largest in India, founded in 1680-81
Sela Pass and Sela Lake at about 4,170 m, and the Jaswantgarh war memorial
Bumla Pass on the India-China border and Madhuri (Sangetsar) Lake, with Army permits arranged
Two jeep safaris in Kaziranga, home to most of the world's one-horned rhinos
Nohkalikai Falls, Mawsmai Cave and the Seven Sisters Falls at Cherrapunji
Mawlynnong village, the living root bridge at Riwai and the clear Umngot River at Dawki

days.title: Land in Guwahati, gateway to the North East
days.summary: Arrival at Guwahati airport and transfer to the hotel.

rows.label: On landing · Guwahati airport (GAU)
rows.title: Meet your driver
rows.text: Your driver and Innova wait at arrivals for the drive into the city.

rows.label: Evening
rows.title: Optional: Brahmaputra sunset cruise
rows.text: A one-hour cruise from Guwahati's riverfront, when the water level allows.
notes: Cruises stop when the river is high, mostly in the monsoon.

days.note: Your Arunachal Inner Line Permit is ready before you land; keep the PDF on your phone and a printout in the car.

days.title: Up the Brahmaputra to the foothills of Bhalukpong
days.summary: Drive to Bhalukpong with an optional dolphin boat ride at Bhomoraguri near Tezpur.

rows.label: About 08:00
rows.title: Leave Guwahati after breakfast
rows.text: North-east along the Brahmaputra plains.

rows.label: Late morning · Bhomoraguri, Tezpur
rows.title: Gangetic river dolphin boat ride (optional)
rows.text: Local boatmen take you out on the Brahmaputra to watch for the endangered river dolphin.
notes: Tickets are sold by the forest department one day ahead and depend on the water level.

rows.label: Afternoon
rows.title: Bhalukpong and the Kameng River
rows.text: Cross into Arunachal at the Bhalukpong check-post. Evening at the riverside cottages.

days.note: The ILP is checked at Bhalukpong. Keep it and your original ID handy at the check-post.

days.title: Orchids of Tipi and the climb to Dirang
days.summary: Drive to Dirang via the Tipi Orchid Centre and Sessa.
strip: Orchids bloom late March to May

rows.label: Morning
rows.title: Tipi Orchid Research Centre
rows.text: Glasshouses with hundreds of Himalayan orchid species, a short stop on the highway.

rows.label: Afternoon
rows.title: Through Bomdila to Dirang
rows.text: The road winds up the Kameng valley through pine and rhododendron forest.
notes: Mountain roads in Arunachal can close for a few hours after landslides. We keep buffer time in every road day.

rows.label: Evening
rows.title: Check in at Awoo Resort
rows.text: Apple and kiwi orchards around the valley.

days.note: Drink plenty of water from today. Dirang is the first step of acclimatisation before Tawang at 3,000 m.

days.title: Dirang valley, Mandala Top and Sangti
days.summary: Mandala Top, Dirang Dzong and monastery, and the Monpa villages of Sangti Valley.

rows.label: Morning
rows.title: Mandala Top
rows.text: A ridge of 108 stupas with wide views of the Himalaya.

rows.label: Midday
rows.title: Dirang Dzong and Dirang Monastery
rows.text: A 17th-century stone fort village, still lived in by Monpa families.
notes: Cover shoulders and walk clockwise around stupas and prayer wheels.

rows.label: Afternoon
rows.title: Sangti Valley
rows.text: A broad river valley of fields and Monpa homesteads. Black-necked cranes winter here from November to February.

days.note: This easy day is deliberate. Walk slowly and sleep well: tomorrow you cross Sela at about 4,170 m.

days.title: Over Sela Pass to Tawang
days.summary: Drive to Tawang over Sela Pass, with the Jaswantgarh war memorial on the way.

rows.label: Morning
rows.title: Sela Pass and Sela Lake
rows.text: The road now has the Sela Tunnel, but in good weather we drive over the old pass for the frozen lake and prayer flags.
notes: Snow can close the pass road in winter; the tunnel keeps the route open. Spend no more than 20 to 30 minutes at the top.

rows.label: Midday
rows.title: Jaswantgarh War Memorial
rows.text: A memorial to Rifleman Jaswant Singh Rawat, who held this ridge in 1962. The Army canteen serves hot tea and snacks.

rows.label: Afternoon
rows.title: Arrive Tawang
rows.text: Check in and rest.

days.note: Pack a down jacket, gloves and a cap in the car today, whatever the season.

days.title: Tawang Monastery, Urgelling and the War Memorial
days.summary: Tawang Monastery, Urgelling Monastery and the Tawang War Memorial.

rows.label: Morning
rows.title: Tawang Monastery (Galden Namgey Lhatse)
rows.text: Founded in 1680-81, home to about 450 monks and an 8-metre gilded Buddha. Visit the museum and library.
notes: Cover arms and legs, remove hats inside the prayer hall and never point your feet at the altar.

rows.label: Midday
rows.title: Urgelling Monastery
rows.text: Birthplace of the Sixth Dalai Lama, a quiet small temple below the town.

rows.label: Afternoon
rows.title: Tawang War Memorial
rows.text: A 27-foot stupa-style memorial to the soldiers of 1962. The evening light-and-sound show runs most days.

days.note: Your Bumla permit is applied for today at the Deputy Commissioner's office with your ID, ready for tomorrow.

days.title: Bumla Pass and Madhuri Lake
days.summary: Bumla Pass on the India-China border, Sangetsar (Madhuri) Lake and PTso Lake, in a local permitted vehicle.
strip: About 37 km each way, rough road

rows.label: About 07:00
rows.title: Local taxi to Bumla
rows.text: Only locally registered vehicles may go beyond Tawang, so we switch to a Tata Sumo or similar.
notes: Bumla is open to Indian citizens only, with a permit, and is closed on some days for Army reasons. Foreign guests do the lakes only.

rows.label: Morning
rows.title: Bumla Pass
rows.text: The Army shows you the border post and tells the story of 1962. Photography is allowed only where they say.

rows.label: Midday
rows.title: Sangetsar (Madhuri) Lake
rows.text: A lake formed by the 1950 earthquake, with tree trunks still standing in the water. The Army café sells momos and tea.

rows.label: Afternoon
rows.title: PTso Lake and Ani Gompa
rows.text: A photo stop at PTso on the way back, then a nunnery above town.

days.note: Children under 10 and anyone with heart or breathing conditions should skip Bumla and keep to the lakes.

days.title: Back over the mountains to Bomdila
days.summary: Drive to Bomdila and visit the upper and lower monasteries.

rows.label: Morning
rows.title: Leave Tawang after breakfast
rows.text: Back over Sela, or through the tunnel in bad weather.

rows.label: Afternoon
rows.title: Gontse Rabgyaling (Upper Gompa) and Lower Gompa
rows.text: Monasteries with views over the Kameng ranges.

rows.label: Evening
rows.title: Bomdila market
rows.text: Monpa carpets, yak-wool shawls and thangkas.

days.note: Today is the last high-altitude night. From here you go down to the plains.

days.title: Down to the grasslands of Kaziranga

rows.label: About 07:00
rows.title: Leave Bomdila
rows.text: Down through Bhalukpong and across the Brahmaputra plains.

rows.label: Afternoon
rows.title: Arrive at Diphlu River Lodge
rows.text: Cottages on stilts facing paddy fields.

days.note: Tomorrow's safari slots are confirmed tonight. The forest department releases them the evening before.

days.title: Rhinos, elephants and swamp deer in Kaziranga
days.summary: Morning and afternoon jeep safaris in two ranges of Kaziranga National Park.
strip: Park open about November to April

rows.label: About 07:00
rows.title: Jeep safari, Central (Kohora) range
rows.text: Open grassland with rhinos, wild buffalo, swamp deer and elephants, often at close range.
notes: Safaris run only when the park is open, usually 1 November to 30 April. The elephant ride is optional and depends on forest permission.

rows.label: About 13:30
rows.title: Jeep safari, Western (Bagori) range
rows.text: The densest rhino area of the park.

rows.label: Evening
rows.title: Kaziranga Orchid and Biodiversity Park
rows.text: Hundreds of orchid species and an Assamese food court.

places: Kaziranga National Park Central Range Kohora
Kaziranga National Orchid and Biodiversity Park
days.note: Wear earthy colours, keep voices low and never step out of the jeep. Carry a scarf for the dust.
route: Kaziranga National Park Central Range Kohora
Kaziranga National Orchid and Biodiversity Park

days.title: Through Assam to the hill capital of Shillong
days.summary: Drive to Shillong with a stop at Umiam Lake.

rows.label: Morning
rows.title: Drive south to Meghalaya
rows.text: Through tea gardens and the Guwahati bypass.

rows.label: Afternoon
rows.title: Umiam Lake
rows.text: A wide reservoir among pine hills, 15 km before Shillong.

rows.label: Evening
rows.title: Police Bazaar
rows.text: Shillong's lively centre.

days.note: Meghalaya's caves and falls are at their best after the rains, from September to November.

days.title: Cherrapunji: waterfalls and caves
days.summary: Day trip to Cherrapunji (Sohra): Elephant Falls, Mawsmai Cave, Seven Sisters Falls and Nohkalikai Falls.

rows.label: Morning
rows.title: Elephant Falls
rows.text: Three-tier falls just outside Shillong.

rows.label: Midday
rows.title: Mawsmai Cave
rows.text: A short lit limestone cave. Narrow in places, with some stooping.
notes: Shoes with grip; the floor is wet.

rows.label: Afternoon
rows.title: Seven Sisters Falls and Nohkalikai Falls
rows.text: Nohkalikai drops about 340 m, one of the tallest plunge falls in India.
notes: Many falls thin out from January to March.

days.note: Carry a light rain jacket even in winter: clouds roll in fast in Sohra.

days.title: Mawlynnong, the living root bridge and Dawki
days.summary: Mawlynnong village, the Riwai living root bridge and the clear Umngot River at Dawki.

rows.label: Morning
rows.title: Mawlynnong
rows.text: A tidy Khasi village famous for cleanliness, with a bamboo skywalk over the forest.

rows.label: Late morning
rows.title: Riwai living root bridge
rows.text: Roots of rubber fig trees trained by the Khasi people into a walkable bridge. About 10 minutes down steps.
notes: Steps are slippery after rain. Hold the railings.

rows.label: Afternoon
rows.title: Umngot River, Dawki
rows.text: A boat ride on water so clear the boats seem to float. The Bangladesh border is right here.
notes: The water is clearest from November to April. Boats are paid locally.

rows.label: Evening
rows.title: Back to Shillong
rows.text: About 3 to 4 hours.

days.note: Carry a packed lunch today; restaurants are few on this road.

days.title: Back to Guwahati and the Kamakhya temple
days.summary: Drive to Guwahati with Kamakhya Temple and an optional river cruise.

rows.label: Late morning
rows.title: Kamakhya Temple
rows.text: One of India's most revered Shakti peethas, on Nilachal Hill.
notes: Queues are long on Tuesdays, Saturdays and festival days. A VIP entry ticket is sold at the temple.

rows.label: Evening
rows.title: Optional Brahmaputra sunset or dinner cruise
rows.text: When the water level allows.

days.note: Tonight, pack your bags and keep the ILP and ID in your hand luggage for the airport.

days.title: Fly home from Guwahati

rows.label: Morning
rows.title: Transfer to the airport
rows.text: Reach the airport 2 hours before a domestic flight.

days.note: Thank you for travelling the North East with us.

best_time: October to April. October to December gives the clearest mountain views; Kaziranga opens in November; March and April bring rhododendrons and orchids. Avoid June to September, when monsoon landslides close the Arunachal roads and Kaziranga is shut.
seasons: Clear, cold nights, about 15° / 2° in Tawang. Sela can see snow from December.
Kaziranga safaris, rhododendrons in spring, waterfalls thinner in Meghalaya.

faqs.q: How high does this tour go, and is altitude a problem?
faqs.a: Tawang is at about 3,000 m, Sela Pass about 4,170 m and Bumla about 4,600 m. Two nights in Dirang first help you adjust. Walk slowly, drink water, and tell us about any heart, lung or blood-pressure condition before you book.

faqs.q: Can foreign nationals do this tour?
faqs.a: Yes, with a Protected Area Permit for Arunachal, which we arrange. Bumla Pass is open only to Indian citizens, so foreign guests visit the lakes instead.
Usually from 1 November to 30 April. Outside those months we replace the safaris with tea-garden and village visits.
Yes. A 10-night version skips Bhalukpong and one Shillong night, or you can do Arunachal and Kaziranga only in 9 nights.

faqs.q: Can this itinerary be changed for our dates and pace?
faqs.a: Yes. Every Blue Diamond Voyage itinerary is a starting point. We change the number of nights, the hotels, the pace and the activities to suit your family, and send you a personalised quote.

price_note: Contact us for a personalised quote for your dates, flights and hotel choice.
entry_notes: Carry the original photo ID, not a photocopy. Security at airports and many temples checks it.
Phone and internet: Jio and Airtel work best across most of this route. Download offline Google Maps before hill or forest stretches, where signal drops.

good_to_know.title: UPI, cards and cash
good_to_know.text: UPI works almost everywhere, even at small stalls. Keep some cash in INR 100 and 200 notes for temples, parking, tips and places where the network is weak.

good_to_know.title: Temple and shrine etiquette
good_to_know.text: Cover shoulders and knees. Remove shoes where asked, and carry socks for hot stone floors. Leather belts and bags are not allowed inside some Jain and Hindu temples. Ask before photographing people and inside shrines.

good_to_know.title: Water and street food
good_to_know.text: Drink sealed bottled or filtered water only. Choose busy stalls where food is cooked in front of you, and skip cut fruit and ice from roadside stalls.

good_to_know.title: Driving times
good_to_know.text: Indian roads are slower than the kilometres suggest: plan on 40 to 50 km an hour on highways and much less in hills and towns. Your driver's breaks and meal stops are built into the timings.

good_to_know.title: Plugs and tipping
good_to_know.text: Plugs are Indian three-pin and two-pin, 230 volts. Tipping drivers and guides about INR 300 to 500 a day is appreciated.

dining_intro: India is the easiest country in the world for vegetarian and Jain travellers. We send your dietary brief to every hotel, and your driver knows clean, pure-vegetarian restaurants on each road day.
dining_avoid: Ask for food cooked fresh and tell the kitchen clearly if you eat Jain: no onion, garlic, ginger, potato or other root vegetables. Many dishes start with an onion-garlic base even when the menu says vegetarian.
food_card: Hum shuddh shakahari (Jain) hain. Pyaz, lahsun, adrak, aloo, gajar ya koi bhi zameen ke neeche ki sabzi nahi. Ande nahi. Kripya taaza banaiye. Dhanyavaad.
